signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hormuz Supply Shock
signals.text: Strait of Hormuz naval mine detonations and tanker fire lift WTI crude to $104.1/bbl, driving massive outperformance in petro-currency NOK against an energy-import dependent EUR. Crude supply dislocation fuels the G10 theme spread where NOK leads at +1.681% (n=2 pairs) versus EUR lagging at -0.584% (n=9 pairs), reinforced by Fitch's unscheduled French sovereign outlook downgrade and an extreme 2.265% spread gap. Monday open gap risk favors NOK extension as European trade balances absorb higher energy import costs. Trade bias: Bullish NOK against EUR into the Tokyo and London open. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo market open and Asian crude trade reaction following the Strait of Hormuz escalation. Risk: Immediate diplomatic breakthrough in Doha talks or de-escalation statements reopening transit lanes.
evidence: Strait of Hormuz tanker ignited by naval mines

signals.title: EUR/USD — Extreme Net-Short Positioning vs French Downgrade
signals.text: EUR COT LF short -99.6k (pctl 2, z -1.78) anchors crowded downside positioning as EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.1166 below all major moving averages. Deteriorating Eurozone macro sentiment following Fitch's unscheduled French sovereign outlook downgrade and ESI divergence sustains heavy downside momentum toward 1.1100. Monday's German retail sales and US ISM Manufacturing determine if macro divergence triggers fresh lows or induces a squeeze against the 150bp SOFR-€STR yield disadvantage. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD with short positions favored on intraday bounces below 1.1201. Catalyst: German Retail Sales at 07:00 UTC followed by US ISM Manufacturing PMI at 15:00 UTC on Monday. Risk: US ISM manufacturing contraction below 50.0 triggering a squeeze of extreme leveraged EUR shorts.

supports: technical regime points with the stated direction

signals.title: USD/CAD — BoC Tightening Divergence vs Extreme CAD Short
signals.text: CAD COT LF short -97.0k (15.1% long, pctl 8, z -1.55) leaves USD/CAD vulnerable to an acute short-squeeze unwind after Friday's close at 1.3973 below its 20-day SMA of 1.4123. The Bank of Canada's active hiking cycle to 2.50% combined with WTI crude breaking above $104/bbl compresses North American terms-of-trade divergence. US ISM Manufacturing on Monday tests the dollar's +145bp SOFR-CORRA carry support against an extended CAD short cover. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD targeting a break below 1.3900 as crowded CAD shorts cover. Catalyst: US ISM Manufacturing PMI and Prices Paid releases on Monday at 15:00 UTC. Risk: US ISM headline surprise above 56.0 reinforcing Fed-BoC rate divergence and reviving USD demand.
evidence: Carry: SOFR 3.94% vs CORRA 2.49% (+145bp USD advantage)

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Advantage Clashes with Downside Put Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY closed Friday at 157.52, underpinned by a massive +271bp SOFR over TONA carry cushion that faces resistance from a heavy -2.24 risk reversal put skew. Geopolitical risk in the Persian Gulf and tech-driven equity volatility elevate hedging demand for the yen despite the 279bp 2Y sovereign yield gap. The US ISM manufacturing report and broad Treasury yields determine whether carry flows can overcome safe-haven repatriation pressure. Trade bias: Range-bound USD/JPY between 156.80 and 158.20 as carry yield offsets haven demand. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 70% hike priced) on 18 Dec following Monday's US ISM Manufacturing PMI at 15:00 UTC. Risk: Sharp spike in US 10Y yields above 5.00% that forces a liquidation of JPY downside options hedges.
evidence: Carry: SOFR 3.94% vs TONA 1.23% (+271bp USD advantage)
